Also define the ScenarioTestManifest and ScenarioTestManifestEntry types in the same file for the manifest JSON: ScenarioTestManifest has Scenarios []ScenarioTestManifestEntry; ScenarioTestManifestEntry has Name string and TestFile string (json tags: 'name' and 'test_file').

Implement WriteScenarioTestsStage in internal/next/specloop/stages/write_scenario_tests.go. Follow the WriteContractsStage pattern exactly. The stage: (1) Name() returns 'write_scenario_tests'. (2) Config struct: WriteScenarioTestsStageConfig with SpecPath, EvidenceDir, WorkDir, Store fields. (3) Constructor: NewWriteScenarioTestsStage(writer ScenarioTestWriter, cfg WriteScenarioTestsStageConfig, budget *specloop.Budget, eventLog *runstore.EventLog). (4) Run logic: a) If rs.ScenarioTestsWritten is true, return Continue (idempotency). b) Parse scenarios from spec using contract.ParseScenarios. c) If no scenarios, return Continue. d) Collect implFiles from rs.Tasks where Status=='done', deduplicating FilesChanged into a unique sorted set. e) Read existing manifest from EvidenceDir/scenario-test-manifest.json if it exists. f) For each scenario: check budget (return Blocked if exhausted with scenario_tests_blocked event), check if scenario already in manifest and test file exists and compiles via 'go test -c -o /dev/null ./<package-path>' — if so skip it. Otherwise call writer.WriteScenarioTest with empty compileErrors. Run compile check on returned testFilePath. On compile failure, retry up to 2 times calling WriteScenarioTest with compile error output as compileErrors. If all 3 attempts fail, emit scenario_tests_blocked event and return Blocked. On success, update manifest file incrementally (append entry, write JSON), emit scenario_tests_written event. g) After all scenarios, set rs.ScenarioTestsWritten = true, emit scenario_tests_complete event, return Continue. The compile check command: 'go test -c -o /dev/null ./<package-path>' where package-path is derived from the testFilePath directory relative to WorkDir. Use os/exec.CommandContext for compile checks.

Implement FailureHistory helper functions as exported functions in internal/next/specloop/failure_history.go (new file). Functions: (1) ExtractTestFailureKeys(output string) []string — extracts test function names from 'go test' output by matching lines matching '--- FAIL: TestFunctionName' (regex: `--- FAIL: (\S+)`). (2) ExtractContractFailureKeys(failures []string) []string — extracts contract keys from failure messages formatted as 'contract:<scenario-name> — <details>' by splitting on ' — ' and taking the first segment. (3) UpdateFailureHistory(history map[string]int, currentFailures []string) map[string]int — for each key in currentFailures, increment count; for each key in history NOT in currentFailures, reset to 0 (delete from map). (4) AnnotateWithPersistentHints(failures []string, history map[string]int, threshold int) []string — for each failure whose key has history[key] >= threshold, append the diagnostic hint string 'persistent-failure: <key> has failed N consecutive cycles — may indicate a bad test specification rather than an implementation bug'. Return new slice with annotated failures.
